evals.prompt: Define a dark mode implementation in 2-3 sentences. Name the concerns it handles.
expected_elements: It is a two-state runtime switch over an already-designed palette, not a palette design task
Names the five concerns: detection, apply-before-paint, runtime propagation, asset variants, browser-chrome hints
Each concern has a defined web-platform primitive
States it consumes a palette designed elsewhere (color-system-design)

evals.prompt: How does theme detection work, and why is 'System' a distinct third state rather than 'no preference saved'?
expected_elements: prefers-color-scheme media query reflects the OS/browser preference (window.matchMedia)
Three user choices: System (defers to media query), Light, Dark (override)
The explicit choice is persisted (localStorage/cookie) and outranks the OS
System is a real third state the user can select, not merely the absence of a saved override

evals.prompt: Compare paired :root / [data-theme=dark] custom properties with the CSS light-dark() function for declaring both schemes. When does each fit?
expected_elements: light-dark(a, b) declares both schemes inline and the UA picks based on color-scheme
light-dark() reduces boilerplate for simple cases and is supported in current browsers
Paired :root and [data-theme=dark] custom-property assignments remain typical for token-driven systems
color-scheme must be set for light-dark() (and native controls) to resolve correctly

evals.prompt: A dark-mode user sees a white flash for a moment on cold page load. What causes it and how is it fixed?
expected_elements: Flash-of-incorrect-theme: the browser paints the light default before the persisted dark preference is applied
Fix: a small blocking inline script in <head> reads the persisted preference and sets a class/data attribute on <html> synchronously before stylesheets resolve
SSR frameworks must serialize the resolved theme into the HTML response (often reading a cookie on the server)
Verify by throttling the network and watching the first paint

evals.prompt: How do you handle color-sensitive assets — brand-color raster images, SVG illustrations, the favicon, and embedded media — across themes?
expected_elements: Raster images: dark variants via <picture> with <source media=(prefers-color-scheme: dark)> or CSS background swapping
SVGs: currentColor or CSS custom properties for fill/stroke so they update automatically
Favicon: a dark variant via <link rel=icon media=(prefers-color-scheme: dark)>
Embedded videos/iframes often take their own theme parameter passed via URL

evals.prompt: A teammate asks the dark-mode-implementation skill to choose the actual dark palette values and verify their contrast ratios. Is that in scope? Why or why not?
expected_elements: Not in scope — choosing the dark palette and its contrast pairings is color-system-design
This skill consumes those tokens; it owns the runtime switch, not the color decisions
Contrast-criterion verification is a11y; the palette decisions come from color-system-design
Correctly distinguishes runtime wiring from palette/contrast design

evals.prompt: A developer says 'dark mode is just a CSS re-skin — add a [data-theme=dark] selector and override the colors.' Correct the mental model.
expected_elements: Dark mode is a runtime integration, not a stylesheet swap
CSS-only misses the flash-of-incorrect-theme (needs a pre-paint script or server-serialized theme)
Misses color-scheme for native controls, real dark asset variants, the favicon, and meta theme-color for mobile chrome
Dark mode is a parallel design surface — shadows, focus rings, chart palettes need rethinking; persistence with explicit-over-system

evals.prompt: What would you check to verify a dark mode implementation is complete and correct?
expected_elements: No flash of incorrect theme on cold load (throttle network, watch first paint)
color-scheme declared on :root so native controls render correctly; meta theme-color paired light/dark
Brand-color images and the favicon have dark variants; embedded media themed
The user's explicit choice persists across reloads; all interactive states (focus/hover/selected) visible and contrast-compliant in dark
